headline: Revolution is rapid, fundamental change—when gradual evolution isn't fast enough
universal_truth: Systems that can't adapt gradually eventually break and reform suddenly; change is inevitable, form is not
fun_facts: Most revolutions fail or produce unexpected results—the French Revolution led to Napoleon, not democracy
The Industrial Revolution changed more about daily life in 100 years than the previous 1,000
Technological revolutions are accelerating—the time between major shifts keeps shrinking
discussion_questions: What in your life has changed suddenly rather than gradually?
When is revolution necessary versus destructive?
How do you prepare for rapid change?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: For centuries, nothing much changed. Your life looked like your grandparents' lives. Then: industrial revolution, digital revolution, information revolution—each one faster than the last. Sudden, fundamental change is now the norm, not the exception.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We prefer gradual change—it's easier to adapt. But sometimes systems can't evolve fast enough. What makes revolution happen instead of evolution?

options.text: Revolution happens when pressure for change builds faster than systems can adapt—when gradual evolution is blocked or too slow, sudden transformation becomes inevitable
options.response: Yes. Systems that resist small changes accumulate pressure until they break. Revolution is often the cost of refusing to evolve. Flexibility prevents rupture.

options.text: Revolutions are caused by leaders who drive change
options.response: Leaders matter, but they usually ride waves of accumulated pressure rather than creating them...

q1.title: Pressure Accumulation
q1.script: Revolutions rarely come from nowhere. Pressure builds for years or decades—economic stress, social frustration, technological possibility. What looks sudden was actually slow accumulation reaching critical mass.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Pressure Accumulation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Unpredictable Outcomes
q2.script: Revolutions rarely end where they intended. The French Revolution produced Napoleon. The Russian Revolution produced Stalin. Rapid change is hard to control. Be careful what you wish for when systems break.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Revolution
q3.script: You can experience personal revolution too—sudden life changes, career pivots, relationship shifts. Sometimes gradual change isn't possible. The skill is navigating rapid change without losing yourself.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Systems that can't adapt gradually eventually break and reform suddenly. Change is inevitable; form is not. Build flexibility to avoid rupture.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 211. Tomorrow, we'll explore how life changes over time—evolution. Until then, consider where pressure is building in your life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Pressure Scan - Where Is Change Building?
growTrack.activity: Where in your life is pressure building—frustration, dissatisfaction, need for change that you've been delaying? Can you make gradual changes now, or is revolutionary change becoming necessary? Proactive evolution beats forced revolution.
